question.nlq: Hey! Could you help me list all the folks who are employed at companies that made more than 20 billion in profits, and also show each company's name plus its rank by market value (biggest market value gets rank 1)? I'd love to see the results ordered by that rank.

meanings.gt_sql: SELECT p."Name" AS person_name, c."Name" AS company_name, RANK() OVER (ORDER BY c."Market_Value_in_Billion" DESC) AS market_rank FROM "people" p JOIN "employment" e ON p."People_ID" = e."People_ID" JOIN "company" c ON e."Company_ID" = c."Company_ID" WHERE c."Profits_in_Billion" > 20 ORDER BY market_rank;

turns.sql:
SELECT p.Name AS Person_Name,
       c.Name AS Company_Name,
       RANK() OVER (ORDER BY c.Market_Value_in_Billion DESC) AS Market_Value_Rank
FROM people p
JOIN employment e ON p.People_ID = e.People_ID
JOIN company c ON e.Company_ID = c.Company_ID
WHERE c.Profits_in_Billion > 20
ORDER BY Market_Value_Rank;

WITH ranked_companies AS (
  SELECT
    c.Company_ID,
    c.Name AS Company_Name,
    RANK() OVER (ORDER BY c.Market_Value_in_Billion DESC) AS Market_Value_Rank
  FROM company c
  WHERE c.Profits_in_Billion > 20
)
SELECT
  p.Name AS Person_Name,
  rc.Company_Name,
  rc.Market_Value_Rank
FROM employment e
JOIN ranked_companies rc ON e.Company_ID = rc.Company_ID
JOIN people p ON e.People_ID = p.People_ID
ORDER BY rc.Market_Value_Rank;

WITH ranked_companies AS (
    SELECT
        c."Company_ID",
        c."Name" AS company_name,
        RANK() OVER (ORDER BY c."Market_Value_in_Billion" DESC) AS market_value_rank
    FROM "company" c
    WHERE c."Profits_in_Billion" > 20
)
SELECT
    p."Name" AS person_name,
    rc.company_name,
    rc.market_value_rank
FROM "employment" e
JOIN "people" p ON e."People_ID" = p."People_ID"
JOIN ranked_companies rc ON e."Company_ID" = rc."Company_ID"
ORDER BY rc.market_value_rank;

WITH filtered AS (
  SELECT c.Company_ID, c.Name AS Company_Name, c.Market_Value_in_Billion
  FROM company c
  WHERE c.Profits_in_Billion > 20
),
ranked AS (
  SELECT f.Company_ID, f.Company_Name,
         ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY f.Market_Value_in_Billion DESC) AS Market_Value_Rank
  FROM filtered f
)
SELECT p.Name AS Person_Name, r.Company_Name, r.Market_Value_Rank
FROM employment e
JOIN people p ON e.People_ID = p.People_ID
JOIN ranked r ON e.Company_ID = r.Company_ID
ORDER BY r.Market_Value_Rank;

SELECT p.Name AS Person_Name, c.Name AS Company_Name, RANK() OVER (ORDER BY c.Market_Value_in_Billion DESC) AS Market_Value_Rank FROM employment e JOIN company c ON e.Company_ID = c.Company_ID JOIN people p ON e.People_ID = p.People_ID WHERE c.Profits_in_Billion > 20 ORDER BY Market_Value_Rank;

question.nlq: Could you tell me, for each industry, the total number of employees, total profit in billions, average profit per employee, the company that has the highest profit per employee, and the cumulative sum of sales in billions when companies are ordered by profit per employee descending within that industry?

meanings.gt_sql:
WITH company_stats AS (
  SELECT
    c."Company_ID",
    c."Name",
    c."Industry",
    c."Profits_in_Billion",
    c."Sales_in_Billion",
    COUNT(DISTINCT e."People_ID") AS employee_count
  FROM "company" c
  LEFT JOIN "employment" e ON c."Company_ID" = e."Company_ID"
  GROUP BY c."Company_ID", c."Name", c."Industry", c."Profits_in_Billion", c."Sales_in_Billion"
),
company_metrics AS (
  SELECT
    "Industry",
    "Name",
    "Profits_in_Billion",
    "Sales_in_Billion",
    employee_count,
    CASE WHEN employee_count = 0 THEN NULL ELSE "Profits_in_Billion" / employee_count END AS profit_per_employee,
    SUM("Sales_in_Billion") OVER (PARTITION BY "Industry" ORDER BY (CASE WHEN employee_count = 0 THEN NULL ELSE "Profits_in_Billion" / employee_count END) DESC
        ROWS UNBOUNDED PRECEDING) AS running_sales
  FROM company_stats
)
SELECT
  "Industry",
  SUM(employee_count) AS total_employees,
  SUM("Profits_in_Billion") AS total_profit,
  CASE WHEN SUM(employee_count) = 0 THEN NULL ELSE SUM("Profits_in_Billion") / SUM(employee_count) END AS avg_profit_per_employee,
  (SELECT "Name" FROM company_metrics cm2 WHERE cm2."Industry" = cm."Industry" ORDER BY cm2.profit_per_employee DESC LIMIT 1) AS top_company,
  MAX(running_sales) AS cumulative_sales
FROM company_metrics cm
GROUP BY "Industry"
ORDER BY "Industry";

WITH company_emp AS (
  SELECT c.Company_ID, c.Name AS Company_Name, c.Industry, c.Sales_in_Billion, c.Profits_in_Billion,
         COUNT(e.People_ID) AS employee_count
  FROM company c
  LEFT JOIN employment e ON c.Company_ID = e.Company_ID
  GROUP BY c.Company_ID, c.Name, c.Industry, c.Sales_in_Billion, c.Profits_in_Billion
),
company_metrics AS (
  SELECT *,
         CASE WHEN employee_count = 0 THEN NULL ELSE Profits_in_Billion / employee_count END AS profit_per_employee
  FROM company_emp
),
industry_agg AS (
  SELECT Industry,
         SUM(employee_count) AS total_employees,
         SUM(Profits_in_Billion) AS total_profit_billion,
         AVG(CASE WHEN employee_count = 0 THEN NULL ELSE Profits_in_Billion / employee_count END) AS avg_profit_per_employee,
         SUM(Sales_in_Billion) AS total_sales_billion
  FROM company_metrics
  GROUP BY Industry
),
ranked AS (
  SELECT *,
         ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY Industry ORDER BY profit_per_employee DESC) AS rn
  FROM company_metrics
)
SELECT i.Industry,
       i.total_employees,
       i.total_profit_billion,
       i.avg_profit_per_employee,
       r_max.Company_Name AS highest_profit_per_employee_company,
       i.total_sales_billion AS cumulative_sales_billion
FROM industry_agg i
LEFT JOIN ranked r_max ON i.Industry = r_max.Industry AND r_max.rn = 1;

WITH emp_cnt AS (
    SELECT e.Company_ID, COUNT(DISTINCT e.People_ID) AS employee_count
    FROM employment e
    GROUP BY e.Company_ID
),
comp AS (
    SELECT c.Industry,
           c.Name AS Company_Name,
           ec.employee_count,
           c.Profits_in_Billion,
           c.Sales_in_Billion,
           (c.Profits_in_Billion * 1.0) / ec.employee_count AS profit_per_employee
    FROM company c
    JOIN emp_cnt ec ON c.Company_ID = ec.Company_ID
),
ind_agg AS (
    SELECT Industry,
           SUM(employee_count) AS total_employees,
           SUM(Profits_in_Billion) AS total_profit,
           (SUM(Profits_in_Billion) * 1.0) / SUM(employee_count) AS avg_profit_per_employee
    FROM comp
    GROUP BY Industry
),
highest AS (
    SELECT Industry, Company_Name AS highest_ppc_company
    FROM (
        SELECT Industry,
               Company_Name,
               profit_per_employee,
               ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY Industry ORDER BY profit_per_employee DESC) AS rn
        FROM comp
    )
    WHERE rn = 1
),
comp_with_cum AS (
    SELECT Industry,
           Company_Name,
           employee_count,
           profit_per_employee,
           Sales_in_Billion,
           SUM(Sales_in_Billion) OVER (PARTITION BY Industry ORDER BY profit_per_employee DESC
                                        ROWS UNBOUNDED PRECEDING) AS cum_sales
    FROM comp
)
SELECT
    cwc.Industry,
    cwc.Company_Name,
    cwc.employee_count AS Employees_Company,
    cwc.profit_per_employee AS Profit_Per_Employee_Company,
    cwc.cum_sales AS Cumulative_Sales,
    ia.total_employees AS Total_Employees_Industry,
    ia.total_profit AS Total_Profit_Industry_Billion,
    ia.avg_profit_per_employee AS Avg_Profit_Per_Employee_Industry,
    h.highest_ppc_company AS Company_Highest_Profit_Per_Employee
FROM comp_with_cum cwc
JOIN ind_agg ia ON cwc.Industry = ia.Industry
JOIN highest h ON cwc.Industry = h.Industry
ORDER BY cwc.Industry, cwc.profit_per_employee DESC;

    SELECT Industry, MAX(Market_Value_in_Billion) as max_market_value
    FROM "company"
    GROUP BY Industry
),
top_companies AS (
    SELECT c.Company_ID, c.Industry, c.Name, c.Market_Value_in_Billion
